question: What permanent ownership and revocation contract should the public requester-scoped MCP resolver API enforce before it ships?
rationale: The code can mechanically implement several models, but only maintainers can choose whether resolver ownership is declaration-bound, conflict-disabled, or intentionally load-order-based and whether a five-minute credential-revocation window is acceptable.

options.title: Bind ownership explicitly
options.body: Associate each resolver with the plugin-owned MCP declaration and disable the scoped server on conflicting ownership; retain the documented five-minute default only with explicit approval.

options.title: Disable all conflicts
options.body: Permit config-declared servers without an owner, but make any cross-plugin duplicate leave that server unavailable until the operator resolves the conflict.

options.title: Accept first registration
options.body: Keep first-registration-wins and formally document plugin load order plus the five-minute revocation window as trusted deployment contracts.

recommendation.title: Bind ownership explicitly
recommendation.body: Associate each resolver with the plugin-owned MCP declaration and disable the scoped server on conflicting ownership; retain the documented five-minute default only with explicit approval.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice defines a permanent public plugin API and an authorization boundary across core, plugins, and Codex harness delivery.
